short: Joint LSTM + pixel front end (M06) is ahead of 2015 lipreading, but pixel-input and recurrent word models predate it, and the 8.3-point gain is over linear SVMs, not HMMs.
position: The paper changes decoding (M06): a feed-forward layer and two LSTM layers trained jointly on mouth crops replace hand-crafted features and a separate classifier [@wand2016lipreading]. Joint training of a gated recurrent model with a pixel-input front end is ahead of its field: of 159 lip-reading studies first public before 2015-07, 113 name an HMM and 2 a recurrent network (pattern match, mentions included, Appendix), and no read prior trains its recurrent model with the front end. Neither pixel input nor recurrent word models are new: a 1994 time-delay network learned from gray-level lip pixels [@duchnowski1994see], and diffusion networks modelled whole words over lip-contour features [@movellan1999diffusion]. The gain holds across the 10 evaluation speakers of one corpus with no seeds, and it is a gain over linear SVMs on a six-frame vector, not over the HMM pipeline of the time, so it shows a new design, not a better one. Pre-cut word clips (M04) and per-speaker splits (M12) are standard, since both alternatives were in common use. The 11.6% gain is relative, 8.3 points absolute (inference).
